questions.q: Why does tempdb represent a third distinct storage profile, separate from data and log?
options: It has extremely high write churn with no durability requirement, since it's rebuilt on every restart
It only ever performs sequential reads
It shares the exact same profile as the transaction log
It never grows once created
questions.explain: tempdb objects are created and dropped constantly and never need to survive a restart, giving it a distinct I/O and durability profile from both data and log files.

questions.q: Why is RAID 10 the standard recommendation for both data and log volumes?
options: It gives strong read and write performance with real redundancy, at the cost of using twice the raw disk capacity
It is the cheapest RAID level in terms of disk usage
It provides no redundancy but the fastest possible writes
It is only suitable for read-only archive filegroups
questions.explain: RAID 10 (striped mirrors) balances strong read/write performance with redundancy — a disk from each mirrored pair can fail without data loss — making it a solid default for both data and log.

questions.q: Why is RAID 5 a poor fit specifically for the transaction log?
options: Every write incurs a parity-calculation penalty, which hurts a write-heavy, latency-sensitive sequential stream
RAID 5 cannot store .ldf files at all
RAID 5 has no capacity efficiency benefit over RAID 10
The log file requires RAID 5 specifically for VLF management
questions.explain: RAID 5's distributed parity adds write overhead on every I/O, which is a poor match for the log's write-heavy, latency-sensitive sequential access pattern, even though it's acceptable for read-heavy data volumes.

questions.q: Why should data, log, and tempdb be placed on separate physical volumes where possible?
options: It isolates I/O contention between them, and a problem on one volume doesn't necessarily take down the others
SQL Server requires separate volumes to start
It only matters for Azure SQL Database, not on-prem instances
It eliminates the need for RAID entirely
questions.explain: Separate volumes (or genuinely separate LUNs) prevent contention between the different I/O patterns of data, log, and tempdb, and provide a degree of fault isolation between them.

questions.q: What is Microsoft's guidance regarding antivirus and SQL Server's data/log files?
options: Exclude the data, log, and backup file paths (and sqlservr.exe) from real-time antivirus scanning
Antivirus should scan every .mdf and .ldf write in real time for maximum security
Antivirus exclusions are unnecessary and have no effect on SQL Server
Only the tempdb path needs an antivirus exclusion
questions.explain: Real-time scanning of SQL Server's data, log, and backup paths can cause performance issues and even file-locking I/O errors mid-write, so Microsoft recommends excluding those paths and the sqlservr.exe process.
